# Temple Scroll Column 20 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 20 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**20:1** Place all of these offerings on the open hands of Aaron and his sons

**20:2** and have them present them as a wave offering before Me.

**20:3** Then take the offerings from their hands and burn them on the altar along with the burnt offering,

**20:4** as a pleasing aroma before Me — a fire offering to the LORD.

**20:5** Take the breast of the ordination ram that belongs to Aaron and present it as a wave offering before Me;

**20:6** this will be your portion.

**20:7** Set apart as holy the breast that was presented and the thigh that was contributed —

**20:8** the portions that were presented and set aside from the ordination ram for Aaron and his sons.

**20:9** These portions will always belong to Aaron and his sons as their rightful share from the Israelites.

**20:10** Carry out the ordination over seven days, offering a young bull each day as a sin offering for purification.

**20:11** Purify the altar by performing atonement on it, then anoint it to make it holy.

**20:12** For seven days perform the atonement rites on the altar to consecrate it,

**20:13** and the altar will become supremely holy — anything that touches it will become holy.

**20:14** Here is what you are to sacrifice on the altar each day without fail: two one-year-old lambs.

**20:15** Offer one lamb in the morning and the second lamb in the evening.

**20:16** With each lamb include a tenth of a measure of fine flour mixed with a quarter-hin of pressed olive oil, along with a quarter-hin of wine as a drink offering.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 20 brings the ordination ceremony to its climax and establishes the daily rhythm of the sanctuary. The wave offering — placing portions on the priests' open hands and presenting them before God — is a powerful visual symbol of priestly mediation. The seven-day consecration period parallels creation itself: seven days to make the sanctuary ready for God's dwelling. The daily offering of two lambs (morning and evening) establishes the heartbeat of the temple's worship life.*
